bib.title: Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
bib.venue: IJCNLP-AACL 2023 (13th IJCNLP and 3rd AACL-IJCNLP, Volume 1: Long Papers)

question: Can a CoT-style pipeline whose answer is produced by deterministically executing the LM-written reasoning chain give faithful explanations without losing accuracy?
hypothesis: Guaranteeing faithfulness (LM translates, deterministic solver answers) does not cost accuracy and may improve it.
contributions: Faithful CoT: Translation (NL query to interleaved NL+symbolic chain) and Problem Solving (deterministic solver) stages
Generalises across Python, Datalog, PDDL and a relational-inference engine over 4 domains; new few-shot SOTA on 7 of 10 datasets
Analysis of LMs, exemplar and phrasing robustness, solver role, human plausibility study and error patterns

method.summary: An LM few-shot prompted with (Q, C, A) exemplars writes a reasoning chain interleaving NL comments (subquestions, dependency graph, support rationales) and task-specific symbolic code; a Python interpreter, Datalog executor, PDDL planner or relation-rule engine executes it to get the answer. Compared with standard, CoT and Least-to-Most prompting under greedy and self-consistency decoding on 10 datasets.
method.task: few-shot multi-step reasoning (math word problems, multi-hop QA, planning, relational inference)

other.note: listed in App A API use only

inference.samples: n=1 greedy; n=40 self-consistency; exemplar robustness: 6 runs (original + 5 resampled prompts)
inference.prompting: Few-shot (Q, C, A) exemplars, 6-10 per dataset (8 for MWP, 6 StrategyQA, 10 Date/Sports, 7 SayCan, 8 CLUTRR); chain interleaves NL subquestions with '(independent|depends on N, support: [...])' and code; AQuA uses a two-step prompt (numeric answer then closest option)

parameters.solver: Python interpreter / Datalog / PDDL planner / transitivity-rule engine from Zhang et al. 2022

other.latency: GSM8K test 3.5h with Codex, 2.3h with GPT-3
other.baseline_fix: Wei et al. exemplar count inconsistent (10 main text vs 6 appendix); baseline rerun with 10

metrics.name: final answer accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match; MWP integers rounded to nearest integer; Boolean exact match for StrategyQA/Sports; SayCan plan correct if among ground-truth plans; string match otherwise

metrics.name: human-rated chain correctness
metrics.definition: Prolific annotators label chains with correct answers as correct / incorrect NL / incorrect SL / flawed question / confused; majority label

baselines: PAL / PoT reimplemented as 'No NL' prompt
eval.protocol: Single run per cell for Table 1, no significance tests; exemplar-set std from 6 runs; human study 100 annotators, >=3 per item, $16/hr, $280 total; errors manually categorised from 100 sampled errors per dataset

availability.data: cleaned test sets and prompts in the repository

prompts.text:
# Q: There are 15 trees in the grove. Grove workers will plant trees in the grove today. After they are done, there will be 21 trees. How many trees did the grove workers plant today?
# To answer this question, write a Python program to answer the following subquestions:
# 1. How many trees are there in the beginning? (independent, support: ["There are 15 trees"])
trees_begin = 15
# 2. How many trees are there in the end? (independent, support: ["there will be 21 trees"])
trees_end = 21
# 3. How many trees did the grove workers plant today? (depends on 1 and 2, support: [])
trees_today = trees_end - trees_begin
# 4. Final Answer: How many trees did the grove workers plant today? (depends on 3, support: [])
answer = trees_today

# Question: How is [Jason] related to [Myrna]?
# To answer this question, we write a program to answer the following subquestions:
# 1. How is [Jason] related to [Guillermina]? (independent, support: ...)
relation(Jason, Guillermina) = grandfather
# 2. ...
relation(Guillermina, Myrna) = daughter
# 3. Final answer: ...
relation(Jason, Myrna) = relation(Jason, Guillermina) @ relation(Guillermina, Myrna)

User query: Bring me something not sweet to eat.
Goal in PDDL:
(:goal
; I need to find a snack
(exists (?s - snack)
(and (not (is-sweet ?s)) (at ?s user))))
See Tables 11, 14, 15; full prompts in the repository.

results.claim: Faithful CoT beats CoT on CLUTRR, absolute accuracy, greedy.
results.table: Table 1, row Faithful CoT (ours), column CLUTRR, Greedy Decoding

results.table: Table 1, row Faithful CoT (ours), column CLUTRR, Self-Consistency Decoding

results.claim: Abstract claim: Faithful CoT outperforms standard CoT on 9 of 10 benchmarks; relative gains 6.3% MWP, 3.4% Planning, 5.5% Multi-hop QA.
results.note: Abstract text is 'relative accuracy gain of 6.3% on Math Word Problems (MWP)' broken across lines
results.quote: with a relative accuracy gain of 6.3% on Math Word Problems (MWP)

results.claim: StrategyQA is the weak spot: Faithful CoT 63.0 vs CoT 72.5 under greedy decoding.
results.table: Table 1, row Faithful CoT (ours), column StrategyQA, Greedy Decoding

results.claim: 29% of StrategyQA errors (where CoT is right and Faithful CoT wrong) are Datalog syntax errors.
Removing the solver (LM predicts the answer itself) drops GSM8K accuracy by 50.8 points.
The nudge line alone adds 31.3 points on CLUTRR (No NL 9.3 vs No NL but nudge 39.6).
Exemplar choice matters little: GSM8K mean over six exemplar sets 71.8, std 0.6.
results.setup: 6 runs (original plus 5 random samples of k=7-10 from 20 annotated examples), greedy

results.claim: With GPT-4 Faithful CoT reaches 95.0 on GSM8K (CoT 64.9, LtM 91.8).
results.table: Table 6, LM gpt-4, row Faithful CoT (ours), column GSM8K

results.claim: GPT-4 Faithful CoT averages 91.6 over five MWP datasets vs CoT 77.1.
results.table: Table 6, LM gpt-4, row Faithful CoT (ours), column Average

results.claim: Human check: 92.0% of correct-answer MWP chains judged fully correct; StrategyQA only 66.7%.
results.setup: 100 chains per domain, >=3 Prolific annotators each, code-davinci-002 greedy
results.note: MWP 92.0, Planning 94.0, Date 87.9, Sports 100.0, Relation 88.0; agreement for StrategyQA only 0.455

results.claim: Concurrent PAL/PoT-style (No NL) prompt is within 2.0 of Faithful CoT on 6 of 10 datasets; Faithful CoT wins on StrategyQA, Sports, CLUTRR.
Enforcing all three dependency constraints (GOU) lowers self-consistency accuracy, e.g. -5.0 on GSM8K.
Few-shot SOTA claimed on 7 of 10 datasets, 95.0+ accuracy on 6 of them (GPT-4 and Codex).
results.quote: sets new SOTA performance on 7 out of the 10 datasets

limits: code-davinci-002 was discontinued on 2023-03-23, so part of the results cannot be replicated without continued access.
Only the Problem Solving stage is faithful; the Translation stage is still opaque.
Faithfulness does not guarantee correctness; chains can be wrong yet reach correct answers (esp. StrategyQA).
No gain on StrategyQA (Datalog sparse in pretraining, 29% syntax errors) and AQuA; Sports is saturated.
NL comments contribute little to accuracy on GSM8K, Date, SayCan; the human-in-the-loop debugging benefit is untested.
Single run per Table 1 cell; baselines rerun on cleaned test sets by the authors; human-eval agreement low on StrategyQA (0.455); SayCan chains annotated by authors.
